answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-backed graph trust: every identity is a vertex that must lock a refundable deposit in an escrow lagoon before it can transact, and its standing grows only through attested work edges from established vertices. A fake identity starts with zero trust and cannot borrow credibility. Creating thousands of Sybils means locking thousands of deposits and earning thousands of trust edges, while detected fraud slashes the stake and severs the edges, like shale splitting along weak layers. The attacker pays per identity; an honest agent pays only once.
